text:
Elaine (sales): quick one — Ashley from FinPlat asked for an attestation that our edge routing + regional fallbacks won't send data outside EU for their POC. they also want the list of subprocessors touching traffic in eu regions. can we confirm by EOD?

Ashley (customer): hi team, we need this for our legal sigoff. POC will run in eu-west1 and eu-central1 only. primary asks: 1) proof that requests stay in eu unless failover triggers, 2) subprocessor list + locations, 3) what's the failover path and what telemetry shows when we hit it. thanks.

James (solutions): noted. couple quick clarifiers: is tenant pinned to eu-only or are you ok with controlled failover to a non-eu warm standby?

Ashley (customer): must be eu-only for data at rest and in transit unless ops-approved DR. for now assume no cross-border for POC.

Miguel (eng-infra): ok. technically we have two modes: tenant-pin (sticky routing to eu clusters) and region-failover (if capacity/health triggers). we can pin the tenant for the POC which keeps requests on eu nodes + eu egress; fallback policies can be disabled.

Tara (security): we'll need to provide subprocessors list + dataflow diagram and short attestation sentence from security. i can draft. Miguel, can you list which infra services touch traffic (load-balancer, vpc nat, metrics collectors)?

Miguel (eng-infra): sure — short list: 1) Redwood Edge Proxy (hosts in eu regions) 2) Regional inference pool (eu-west1, eu-central1) 3) Metrics aggregator (prometheus replica in eu) 4) Logging pipeline (logs forwarded to customer-configured sink; by default stored in eu) 5) KMS calls to managed key (if BYOK used, keys stay in customer region). note: some third-party monitoring agents (SaaS) are optional and not enabled by default.

James (solutions): Ashley — for the POC we can: a) enable tenant pin to eu, b) disable cross-region failover, c) provide subprocessors list + short diagram, d) produce an ops runbook for what to do if capacity constraints hit. is that acceptable?

Ashley (customer): yes that sounds good. we also need a short statement that no packet-level egress leaves EU under that config, and confirmation about which subprocessors have access to payload (e.g., logging/monitoring vendors).

Elaine (sales): action items: Miguel to dump subprocessors + infra list, Tara to draft security attestation, James to capture routing toggle + runbook steps, me to package and send to Ashley + legal. aiming EOD.

Miguel (eng-infra): i will export a one-page CSV: service,name,region,subprocessor,notes. sample rows will include edge-proxy,regional-pool,metrics,logging. will mark any optional SaaS as "not used by default".

Tara (security): drafting attestation. rough text i plan to send: "Redwood Inference confirms that when tenant-pin to EU is enabled and cross-region failover is disabled, data ingress, processing, and standard logs remain within EU-hosted infrastructure and subprocessors. Any deviation (DR or manual failover) is initiated only with customer authorisation." will add signatures and cert links.

James (solutions): also adding snippet for the console toggle and API flags: ```PATCH /v1/tenants/<id>/routing { "tenant_pin": true, "allow_cross_region_failover": false }``` include note: console UI -> Tenant -> Routing -> enable Pin & disable Failover.

Ashley (customer): perfect. one last ask — can you include estimated cost delta for pinning vs default (we expect small perf bump but curious on cost)?

Miguel (eng-infra): will add quick cost note: likely +5-12% on commit usage due to capacity reservation granularity; i'll quantify with typical qps numbers in the doc.

DeployBot: reminder: attach CSVs and attestation to thread or use secure link - do not paste secrets.

Elaine (sales): thanks everyone — i'll collate and send to Ashley by 17:00 UTC. calling out @Tara @Miguel @James for final approvals before send.

Ashley (customer): thank you! :thumbsup:
